body.target_estimand: \(\tau_P(0)\), defined exclusively as the value at zero of the unique continuous extension of \(\mu_{1,P}-\mu_{0,P}\)
body.estimand_functional:
The causal target is \(\tau_P(0)\), already identified from the observed law by \(\mathrm{prop:causal\mbox{-}identification}\).  For \(\kappa=0\), the established data-only functional is the total second-order estimator \(\widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)\) constructed in \(\mathrm{lem:bounded\mbox{-}overlap\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}risk}\).  With \(S=\alpha+\beta\), \(S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), and \(D_\star=1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2S)\), deterministic tuning gives
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \leq R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \leq C\max\left\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\right\}.
\]
Thus the data-only and supplied-propensity risks have the same pure-power rate when \(S\geq S_\star\), including equality without a logarithmic factor.  Below that elbow the displayed upper bound is proved but its matching nuisance lower bound is not.  For \(\kappa>0\), the total first-order functional from \(\mathrm{thm:first\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}upper}\) gives, with \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\),
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}
 \leq R_n(d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \leq C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)},
\]
and the unresolved higher-order local-zero branches are precisely those retained in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\).

sampling_model.design: Known exactly uniform random design on \([0,1]^d\) with \(n\) independent observations.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment probability is strictly positive almost everywhere and equals zero only at \(x=0\) when \(\kappa>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator knows \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) and the uniform design law, but not \(g_P\), \(e_P\), \(\mu_{0,P}\), or \(\tau_P\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give a pointwise Holder-CATE nuisance-smoothness frontier under bounded overlap over a density-qualified design class; the displayed lower construction in Definition 1 uses a covariate density supported on a perforated set.
Theorem 3 bounds a local-polynomial R-learner under bounded estimated propensities and nondegenerate local Gram matrices.
Theorem 2.1 controls the affinity between two convex mixtures when perturbations localize to a measurable partition.
The random-design variance-functional results use local-polynomial U-statistics and a fuzzy lower construction to expose a regression-functional elbow.
Theorem 1 analyzes empirical-Gram higher-order influence-function corrections that remove a covariate-density smoothness requirement for average doubly robust functionals.
Theorem 2 gives near-minimax integrated \(L_1\) rates for random treated and control designs under bounded density ratios and contrast smoothness at most one.
Theorem 1 gives the scalar pointwise regression rate under a regularly varying design density through a local-mass balance.
The weak-overlap results derive thresholded average-effect limit laws and a scalar regression smoothness degradation under propensity-tail restrictions.
Corollary 4 gives pointwise RKHS CATE rates without consistent propensity estimation while retaining a uniform positive overlap parameter.

body.tldr: For the exact local-zero model, the proved supplied-propensity lower bound and total first-order estimator give, for every allowed parameter tuple, \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\leq R_n\leq C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), where \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\).  At bounded overlap \((\kappa=0)\), a new total second-order projection R-learner improves the upper side to \(C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\}\), where \(D_\star=1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta))\), and proves the oracle rate whenever \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), with no logarithm at equality.  Below that elbow only the exact-uniform nuisance converse remains open; for \(\kappa>0\), the higher-order frontier and critical logarithms remain open.

project_justification.gap: The closest published pointwise CATE frontier assumes bounded overlap over a density-qualified design class, and its displayed least-favorable density removes nuisance-bump transition regions.  That construction does not prove a nuisance-dominated lower bound for the singleton uniform design, and no cited result supplies the higher-order local-zero frontier when \(\kappa>0\).
project_justification.niche: The exact uniform law makes the local projection Gram matrix known and permits a total second-order correction without estimating a design density.  This isolates a larger certified oracle-rate region at bounded overlap while leaving the genuinely new rare-treatment geometry visible rather than folding it into a bounded-overlap theorem.
project_justification.fill: The paper constructs a total one-sided second-order projection R-learner and proves, at \(\kappa=0\), the exact-uniform upper bound \(C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\}\).  Together with Theorem 1's supplied-propensity lower bound, this yields the sharp pure-power oracle rate for \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), including equality without a logarithm, while reporting an honest bracket below the elbow and retaining the full \(\kappa>0\) frontier as an explicit obligation.

body.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, Theorems 1--2 and Definition 2 with equation (14), is the closest bounded-overlap pointwise contrast frontier and motivates the localized second-order correction used here.  The present bounded-overlap theorem proves its own exact-uniform upper inequality using the known Lebesgue Gram matrix, but the comparator's density-qualified class and displayed perforated-support lower witness do not establish the below-elbow lower bound on this singleton uniform design.  Accordingly, the honest bracket pairs the new upper bound with Theorem 1's exact-uniform supplied-propensity lower bound.  Kennedy2023DRCATE supplies bounded-overlap local-polynomial R-learner motivation, while LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF and ShenGaoWittenHan2020 motivate higher-order projection corrections.  RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, requires partition-local perturbations and does not directly cover the overlapping smooth frames needed to preserve full support.  GaoHan2020 concerns integrated random-design contrast risk; Gaiffas2005DegenerateDesign concerns scalar pointwise regression under a design zero; Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics concerns weak-overlap average-effect inference and scalar regression; and Kim2026RKHSPointwiseCATE retains a global overlap lower bound.  WagerAthey2018CausalForests and GRFReference motivate the application: the official \(\texttt{grf}\) workflow learns nuisance regressions and uses treatment-balance restrictions, but no claim is made that its causal forest attains the rates proved here.
body.interpretation: At bounded overlap, unknown propensity variation does not change the pointwise CATE rate once the combined nuisance smoothness reaches \(d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), a strictly weaker requirement than the first-order condition \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\).  Below that elbow, the constructed estimator gives the best certified exact-uniform upper rate, but the missing lower experiment prevents declaring a rate penalty.  Near an actual propensity zero \((\kappa>0)\), the theorem does not yet determine whether higher-order contrast smoothing offsets rare treatment, so the result is a benchmark for assessing local precision rather than an attainment claim about an existing causal forest.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The bounded-overlap higher-order upper calculation is now closed, including exact Gram stabilization and both U-statistic variance components.  Its below-elbow converse remains structurally unresolved: with \(S=\alpha+\beta<\gamma\), disjoint partition-local contrast bumps at amplitude \(\delta=\ell^S\) have Holder scale \(\delta\ell^{-\gamma}=\ell^{S-\gamma}\), overlapping smooth squared frames violate the partition-local premise of RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009 and generate shared-sign multi-observation terms, and filling transition holes contributes \(nh^d\delta^2\) at the proposed scale.  For \(\kappa>0\), an upper proof must additionally control rare-treatment projection and stabilization terms, while lower constructions must repair noninteger corner powers and max-norm tie surfaces without deleting support.
body.honest_scope: For \(\kappa=0\), the established result is \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\leq R_n\leq C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\}\), attained on the upper side by a total second-order projection estimator.  It is sharp and equals the supplied-propensity rate whenever \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), with no logarithmic multiplier at equality.  When \(\alpha+\beta<d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), no matching nuisance lower bound is claimed.  For \(\kappa>0\), only the established first-order bracket is claimed; the higher-order upper and lower frontier, critical logarithms, and complete oracle-penalty classification remain open.
